journal:
I've always thought of harvest time as bittersweet, I used to love watching those few weeks of rushing towards the end of summer as farmers raced to bring everything under cover before it turned too wet. I also loved the cooler weather too, that fresh breeze rolling through and the nights drawing in is always a lovely repireve from that relentless summer sun.

However its also when things start getting quieter, the birds are all out looking for food, the colour starts to get lost as the leaves begin to fall in preparation for winter, I guess for me its the knowledge that eventually, everything get quieter and darker and colder until one day, you wonder when the spring will return.

For those dark months after harvest time, I stand there, without crops to watch over, motionless in the low winter sun, looking forward to the day the green returns to the fields.
prompt: A thin, ragged scarecrow stands along in an emptying field as the sun sets, a small crow is perched on one of his arms, facing away from the camera in the distance

music.why: A lone ragged scarecrow in an emptying field at sunset, with a journal calling harvest bittersweet and longing for spring, suggests fond, slightly sad looking back.
